title: Two-sample comparison of means with unequal variances (Welch)
summary: Compares two arms' means without assuming they have the same spread, which is the assumption every other default here quietly makes.
_anova_is_not_in_this_entry: The Learn page it serves covers t-tests AND analysis of variance. This entry is the two-group comparison only. A k-group one-way analysis is a separate fixture and a separate default worth pinning (R's oneway.test does NOT assume equal variance while aov does), and folding it in here would give one entry two estimands and one fixture two jobs.
_paired_is_a_different_entry: repeatedMeasures is false above. Where the two measurements are on the SAME participant the comparison is paired and neither test here applies: an unpaired test on paired data discards the pairing and is usually conservative, sometimes badly so.
pinned_defaults: R: var.equal = FALSE. This IS t.test's default and is named anyway, because it is the default in none of the other three.
Python: equal_var=False. scipy.stats.ttest_ind DEFAULTS TO THE POOLED TEST, so the shortest correct-looking line in Python runs a different test from the shortest correct-looking line in R.
Stata: unequal. The bare ttest is pooled. Stata's nearby `welch` option is a DIFFERENT df formula, not a synonym -- 442.37 against Satterthwaite's 442.16 here, which separates only in small samples.
SAS: nothing to pin. PROC TTEST prints the Pooled and Satterthwaite rows together and the choice is which one the reader takes. The wrong one is printed first.
